newsitem.title: UK: North Sea, Nigerian crude weak, Dated Brent strong.
newsitem.headline: North Sea, Nigerian crude weak, Dated Brent strong.

text.p: North Sea and Nigerian crude premiums remained under pressure from falling refining margins on Thursday, but Dated Brent maintained a premium to November paper in what traders described as an anomaly.
December Brent shed 23 cents at $23.84 per barrel by 1715 GMT.
Physical trade was thin, but in the defining deal of the day, Dated Brent was bought at Dec paper +44 cents.
On the CFD market, next week's dates were valued at Dec paper +11 cents, 33 cents below the Dated Brent trade and widely considered to be a more fundamental valuation of the crude.
"It appears Stasco has a pricing play which keeps Dated at a premium to November paper. It's difficult for some refiners because it means that margins have been squeezed," a refiner said.

Stasco, which is holding around eight cargoes of Brent, failed its fixture of the Hellespont Orpheum on Thursday and traders said the company may reoffer some of the cargoes back into the European market next week.
A U.S. refiner said Stasco was offering Brent in the U.S. Gulf coast below where it was buying it in Europe, after deducting a freight cost. "It's a leverage play, there's no question," he added.
In the Mediterranean, sentiment on the sour crude market was weak as end-October Urals became ever more prompt.
"Two days, no trades. That means the market's weak with end-October barrels lining up," a trader said.
Nigerian markets were also under pressure from weak gas oil prices and an artificially high Dated Brent price, traders said.
Following Wednesday's Qua Iboe trade at Dated Brent +69 cents, Forcados was offered at Dated +80 cents on Thursday, both about 10 cents below premiums earlier this week.
